the ANSI SQL isolation level definitions do not properly characterize several important isolation types and that a new isolation type is needed.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ANSI SQL definitions are inadequate and misleading.
the ANSI SQL definitions of isolation levels fail to capture the essence of the isolation phenomena, and are not sufficient to characterize the isolation types in common use.
Dirty Reads, non-repeatable Reads, and Phantom Reads are not good phenomena for characterizing isolation types; and Snapshot Isolation is a better isolation type than the ANSI SQL-92 isolation types.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phenomena and definitions are not adequate to characterize all isolation levels, that the ANSI SQL definitions are not adequate for characterizing the locking implementations of these levels, and that the phenomena can be better characterized by adding new ones.
the ANSI SQL isolation level definitions are not sufficient to properly characterize the popular implementations, and that the phenomena are not well defined.
the current SQL-92 definition of isolation types is inadequate and that a more precise definition, along with a new isolation level, is needed.
